import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_19/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_19/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_19/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_19/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_19/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_19/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_19/training_6.csv", index_col=0)
source7 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_19/training_7.csv", index_col=0)
source8 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_19/training_8.csv", index_col=0)

# Fix dtypes in source1 and source6 for join keys to avoid merge errors
# Convert 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated' to consistent types (float for Year Inducted, int for others)
# Some columns may be object due to NaNs or mixed types, so convert carefully

def convert_columns(df, col_types):
    for col, typ in col_types.items():
        if col in df.columns:
            if typ == 'float':
                df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce').astype('float64')
            elif typ == 'int':
                # For int columns with NaNs, convert to float first then to Int64 (nullable int)
                df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce')
                # Use nullable integer dtype to keep NaNs
                df[col] = df[col].astype('Int64')
    return df

source1 = convert_columns(source1, {
    'Year Inducted': 'float',
    'Years Waited': 'int',
    '# of Years Nominated': 'int'
})

source6 = convert_columns(source6, {
    'Year Inducted': 'float',
    'Years Waited': 'int',
    '# of Years Nominated': 'int'
})

# Join 1: Join Source9_19_6 and Source9_19_1 on ['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated']
# Because 'Year Inducted' is float, 'Years Waited' and '# of Years Nominated' are Int64 (nullable int), ensure no dtype mismatch
# Use inner join to keep only matching rows

join1 = pd.merge(
    source6,
    source1,
    on=['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated'],
    how='inner',
    suffixes=('_6', '_1')
)

# After join1, columns from source1 are duplicates of join keys, so drop duplicates columns from source1
# Actually, source1 columns are keys only, so no extra columns to keep from source1 besides keys

# Join 2: Join Source9_19_0 and Source9_19_4 on 'Artist'
join2 = pd.merge(
    source0,
    source4,
    on='Artist',
    how='inner'
)

# Join 3: Join Source9_19_3 and Source9_19_2 on 'Artist'
join3 = pd.merge(
    source3,
    source2,
    on='Artist',
    how='inner'
)

# Join 4: Join Source9_19_5 and Source9_19_7 on 'Artist'
join4 = pd.merge(
    source5,
    source7,
    on='Artist',
    how='inner'
)

# Now join all four intermediate joins on 'Artist'
# Start by joining join1 and join2 on 'Artist'
temp = pd.merge(
    join1,
    join2,
    on='Artist',
    how='inner'
)

# Join temp with join3 on 'Artist'
temp = pd.merge(
    temp,
    join3,
    on='Artist',
    how='inner'
)

# Join temp with join4 on 'Artist'
final_df = pd.merge(
    temp,
    join4,
    on='Artist',
    how='inner'
)

# final_df now contains all columns needed, but some columns may be duplicated or have suffixes
# Columns expected in target:
# ['Artist': string,
#  'Year Inducted': float,
#  'Years Waited': integer,
#  '# of Years Nominated': integer,
#  'Inducted By': string,
#  'Influenced': integer,
#  'Certified Units (Millions)': float,
#  'Albums in RS500': integer,
#  'Top 100 Singles': integer,
#  'Highest Position': integer,
#  'Times on Cover of RS': integer,
#  'Score': float,
#  'Spotify': integer]

# Select and rename columns accordingly
# From join1 (source6 + source1): 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated', 'Inducted By'
# From join2 (source0 + source4): 'Certified Units (Millions)', 'Influenced'
# From join3 (source3 + source2): 'Score', 'Spotify'
# From join4 (source5 + source7): 'Albums in RS500', 'Top 100 Singles', 'Highest Position'
# From source8: 'Times on Cover of RS' (not joined yet)

# Join source8 on 'Artist' to add 'Times on Cover of RS'
final_df = pd.merge(
    final_df,
    source8,
    on='Artist',
    how='left'  # left join to keep all artists in final_df
)

# Fix dtypes and fill missing values if any
# Convert columns to correct types

# 'Year Inducted' float
final_df['Year Inducted'] = pd.to_numeric(final_df['Year Inducted'], errors='coerce').astype('float64')

# 'Years Waited' int
final_df['Years Waited'] = pd.to_numeric(final_df['Years Waited'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# '# of Years Nominated' int
final_df['# of Years Nominated'] = pd.to_numeric(final_df['# of Years Nominated'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# 'Inducted By' string, fill NaN with empty string
final_df['Inducted By'] = final_df['Inducted By'].fillna('').astype(str)

# 'Influenced' int
final_df['Influenced'] = pd.to_numeric(final_df['Influenced'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# 'Certified Units (Millions)' float
final_df['Certified Units (Millions)'] = pd.to_numeric(final_df['Certified Units (Millions)'], errors='coerce').astype('float64')

# 'Albums in RS500' int
final_df['Albums in RS500'] = pd.to_numeric(final_df['Albums in RS500'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# 'Top 100 Singles' int
final_df['Top 100 Singles'] = pd.to_numeric(final_df['Top 100 Singles'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# 'Highest Position' int
final_df['Highest Position'] = pd.to_numeric(final_df['Highest Position'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# 'Times on Cover of RS' int, fill NaN with 0 (assuming no covers means 0)
final_df['Times on Cover of RS'] = pd.to_numeric(final_df['Times on Cover of RS'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype('Int64')

# 'Score' float
final_df['Score'] = pd.to_numeric(final_df['Score'], errors='coerce').astype('float64')

# 'Spotify' int
final_df['Spotify'] = pd.to_numeric(final_df['Spotify'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Select columns in target schema order
Target9_19 = final_df[
    ['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated', 'Inducted By', 'Influenced',
     'Certified Units (Millions)', 'Albums in RS500', 'Top 100 Singles', 'Highest Position',
     'Times on Cover of RS', 'Score', 'Spotify']
]

# Save to CSV without index
Target9_19.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_19/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
